title: Command and SQL Injection via fmt.Sprintf
platform_conditions: Go 1.x standard library (os/exec, text/template, database/sql); applies to all build targets
security_mechanism: os/exec does not invoke a shell: Command(name, args...) passes each element as one argv entry, so injection requires the developer to opt in by building a shell string (exec.Command("sh", "-c", fmt.Sprintf(...))) or by letting an input beginning with '-' become an option of the target binary. The same confidence in fmt.Sprintf produces SQL when its output is passed to db.Query, since database/sql placeholders ('?') are the only out-of-band channel. In templates, text/template never escapes and an explicit template.HTML(value) cast tells html/template to trust the value, defeating auto-escaping at exactly the attacker-controlled position.

source_sink_clues.source: Request parameters interpolated into shell command strings, SQL text, or template values cast to template.HTML.
source_sink_clues.sink: exec.Command("sh", "-c", <formatted string>) or unguarded argv elements; db.Query/QueryRow with fmt.Sprintf-built SQL; text/template execution of user data; template.HTML(x) casts feeding html/template output

tracking_guards: Require exec.Command with a fixed executable and the dynamic value as one separate argv argument (no sh -c); require SQL placeholders with args passed separately to Query/Exec; require html/template (not text/template) for HTML output and no template.HTML casts over untrusted values; require '--' or allowlist checks for values that may start with '-'.
not_candidate_when: The command is a constant executable with input as a single argv element and no option-parsing surface, SQL values bind through placeholders, html/template auto-escaping remains in effect with no template.HTML cast, or the interpolated fragment comes from a fixed server-side allowlist.
synthetic_vulnerable_example: query := fmt.Sprintf("SELECT * FROM items WHERE name = '%s'", name)
synthetic_safe_example: row := db.QueryRow("SELECT * FROM items WHERE name = ?", name)
public_references: CWE-89: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in SQL Command — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/89.html
CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/78.html
